tasks.task: Establish site setup and access control
tasks.scope: Set up site perimeter, establish exclusion zones, position barriers, signage, and falling-object protection for occupied building interface.
hazards: fall of barriers, signage, or falling-object protection due to wind or impact
exclusion zone breach by unauthorised person or pedestrian
trip hazard from barrier footings or cable runs across access routes
struck by vehicle during setup if work zone overlaps traffic or loading area
tasks.dominant_hazard: fall of falling-object protection onto person below occupied building
controls: Install perimeter barriers minimum 2 metres from building edge and below fall zone.
Secure all barriers to ground anchors or weighted bases to resist wind force.
Attach warning signs to barriers every 2 metres, visible from occupied building and public access.
Position falling-object protection netting or mesh minimum 1.5 metres above ground level.
Check netting attachment points weekly for wind damage, tear, or sagging.
Establish exclusion zone with locked gate or controlled access point.
Brief all personnel on exclusion zone boundaries before work starts each day.
Clear trip hazards from barrier footings and cable runs across access routes daily.
tell building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow worker or public access until: perimeter barriers are installed and secured, exclusion zone is established and signed, and falling-object protection is certified in place.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not position any falling-object protection near occupied building until: occupied floors below confirmed and access routes identified.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: barrier or netting damaged, detached, or sagging under wind.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unauthorised person or pedestrian breaches exclusion zone.
🛑 STOP WORK if: trip hazard detected on access routes or around barrier footings.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Brief all personnel on exclusion zone, barrier locations, and falling-object risk before each shift.
check falling-object protection weekly and record condition in site log.
Maintain exclusion zone access log; record all entries and brief all visitors on hazards.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before starting
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works before commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement

monitoring.critical_control: Check perimeter barriers secured to ground and falling-object netting attached without tear or sagging.
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start and after each wind event
monitoring.evidence: Daily site checklist signed by supervisor; photographic record of netting condition; barrier installation certificate retained on site.

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Erect scaffolding or position elevated work platform
tasks.scope: Install full-height working scaffold or EWP system to facade per engineering; tie-offs, guardrails, safe access routes.
hazards: fall from height during erection or use — incomplete guardrails or tie-off points
collapse of scaffold due to defective components, poor foundation, or overload
fall of scaffold components or tools during erection
electrocution if scaffold contact with overhead power lines during erection or repositioning
entrapment or crush hazard during EWP boom operation near fixed structures
tasks.dominant_hazard: collapse of scaffold or fall from height during erection and use
controls: Verify scaffolding design and engineering certification before delivery to site.
Check all components for damage, corrosion, or defects before erection starts.
Install base plates on level, compacted ground or approved temporary works foundation.
Erect scaffolding only on competent persons with current scaffolding licence.
Install guardrails and mid-rails to full height as erection progresses—do not leave gaps.
Secure all tie-offs to structural points certified by engineer before workers use levels.
Conduct competent person scaffold check and tag before any work platform use.
Brief all workers on scaffold load limits, guardrail use, and fall arrest points.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow workers on scaffold until: engineer has signed-off inspection tag and guardrails are complete at full height.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not reposition EWP boom near fixed structures until: spotter confirms clearance and exclusion zone is marked.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold component is bent, cracked, or missing bolts.
🛑 STOP WORK if: guardrails or mid-rails are incomplete or damaged.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold sinks, tilts, or shows visible movement or settlement.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain engineer-signed scaffolding design and temporary works plan before erection.
Engage competent scaffolder certified to erect and tag scaffold per AS/NZS 4576.
Record daily visual check and any repairs in site logbook.
Brief site supervisor and foreman on tie-off locations and load limits before work starts.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Fall-arrest harness and lanyard when working at heights above 2 m during erection

monitoring.critical_control: Check tag on scaffold for engineer sign-off and date before work each day.
monitoring.frequency: Before each shift start and after any modification
monitoring.evidence: Dated inspection tag visible on scaffold, logbook record of check, sign-off by competent scaffolder

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.task: Remove green wall and soft landscaping
tasks.scope: Strip existing green wall system, substrate, and associated fixings from facade; bag and remove debris.
hazards: fall from height if worker loses balance on scaffold or platform during strip
struck by falling green wall substrate, frames, or fixings during removal
minor cut or laceration from sharp fixing brackets, wire, or metal frames
tasks.dominant_hazard: fall from height or struck by falling debris
controls: Wear safety harness clipped to fixed anchor point before starting work at height.
Check scaffolding tag and certification current before using as work platform.
Barricade fall zone below work area to prevent struck-by incidents.
Wear eye protection
Remove fixings and frames in downward sequence to prevent load shift.
Bag all debris in sealed containers during removal to contain dust and plant material.
Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling metal frames and bracket fixings.
Stop work if harness attachment point becomes damaged or compromised.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker loses balance or harness tension increases — assess anchor point integrity immediately
🛑 STOP WORK if: debris falls into occupied area below — resume only after barricade verified and area cleared
🛑 STOP WORK if: respiratory irritation or coughing detected — ventilate area and check dust mask seal
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Brief all workers on fall prevention and barricade zone before starting.
Record daily scaffold tag check and harness inspection in site log.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Safety harness with shock absorber and certified lanyard (anchor tested to 12 kN minimum)
P2 dust mask or respiratory protection (if dust generation exceeds nuisance level)

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone marked, barriers in place, no pedestrians below work area
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start and continuous visual check during work
monitoring.evidence: Daily site log entry; photographic record of anchor point; harness inspection tag dated and signed

responsibility.SUP: Verify fall protection, check module weights, sign off hold points
responsibility.WKR: Wear fall harness, check lanyard attachment, report equipment damage

tasks.task: Carry out crack stitching and sealant application
tasks.scope: Identify structural cracks; install crack stitches where required; apply sealant to joints, gaps, and openings per specification
hazards: fall from height if worker loses balance while working on facade at height
eye irritation or chemical burn from sealant contact during application
respiratory irritation from sealant fumes in enclosed or poorly ventilated areas
minor cut from handling crack stitch bars or sharp sealant application tools
controls: Wear fall arrest harness with lanyard secured to fixed anchor point before starting work at height.
Check all crack stitch bars for sharp edges and burrs; file smooth before use.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection
Apply sealant in well-ventilated areas only; open windows or use mechanical ventilation.
Wear respiratory protective equipment if sealant fumes are visible or smell strong.
Wipe sealant from skin and tools immediately using cloth; do not allow contact with eyes.
Identify crack location and depth using probe or measuring tool before stitching.
Stop work and request engineering assessment if cracks are >5mm wide or show fresh movement.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply sealant until: crack surface is clean, dry, and free of dust and debris
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not work at height until: fall arrest system is fitted and anchor point confirmed as fixed and load-rated
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker reports eye irritation, burning sensation, or difficulty breathing after sealant contact
🛑 STOP WORK if: harness, lanyard, or anchor point shows damage, corrosion, or movement
🛑 STOP WORK if: crack shows fresh spalling, active movement, or structural distress during inspection
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm scaffold or access platform has been tagged and certified before use.
Provide product safety data sheets for all sealants on site and review with workers.
Record crack location, depth, and width in site log before and after treatment.
Arrange first aid kit stocked with eyewash and clean water on site during sealant work.
Brief supervisor on any cracks >5mm or showing structural concern before proceeding.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start and before each height change
monitoring.evidence: Visual inspection of harness fit, anchor point load rating, lanyard condition; supervisor sign-off in site log

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.scope: Remove and rebuild failed brickwork sections; rake out and repoint mortar joints to match existing bond and colour.
hazards: fall from height if worker loses balance on scaffold during brick removal or installation
struck by falling brick, mortar debris, or tools during removal or laying
dust inhalation from cutting or grinding mortar joints
hand or finger crush injury when handling or positioning bricks
collapse of weakened wall section if multiple courses removed without adequate propping or support
tasks.dominant_hazard: collapse of load-bearing wall or fall from height
controls: Install temporary props or shoring to support wall above work zone before removing brick courses.
Check scaffold is tagged by competent person and stable before positioning workers on it.
Remove mortar from joints using grinder with local exhaust ventilation or wet cutting method only.
Wear dust mask P2 when grinding mortar joints or cutting brick.
Barricade work zone below scaffold to exclude public and prevent struck-by incidents.
Hand-position each brick carefully to prevent crush injury; use tongs or grabbers where practicable.
Stop and support wall immediately if cracks appear or mortar falls from untouched joints above work.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start repointing until: removed brickwork is fully rebuilt and mortar has cured per engineer specification (typically 7 days for structural bond).
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: cracks appear in wall or mortar falls from joints above the work zone — do not resume until engineer inspects and approves.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold is not tagged or shows visible damage, movement, or misalignment.
🛑 STOP WORK if: barricade is breached or public enters work zone below scaffold.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Record daily check of props, scaffold tags, and wall condition in site logbook.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Dust mask P2 or powered respirator when grinding mortar
Fall arrest harness with shock absorber and double-lanyard when working at height on scaffold above 2 m

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Each shift start and continuously during removal phase
monitoring.evidence: Daily site logbook entry confirming prop condition, photo record of wall condition, engineer inspection sign-off on rebuild completion

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.task: Repair concrete spalling and prepare surfaces
tasks.scope: Remove spalled concrete; repair with patching compound; grind and clean all masonry and concrete surfaces ready for painting.
hazards: fall from height if worker loses balance on scaffold during spall removal or surface preparation
eye irritation or injury from concrete dust or flying fragments during grinding or chipping
respiratory irritation from silica dust during concrete surface preparation and grinding
struck by falling spalled concrete pieces or grinding debris
vibration white finger from prolonged use of handheld grinder or impact tools
tasks.dominant_hazard: fall from height or respiration hazard from silica dust
controls: Wear eye protection
Wear respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum) during concrete grinding and surface preparation.
Use wet grinding method or dust extraction on angle grinder to control silica dust.
Secure all tools and equipment on scaffold to prevent dropped objects.
Work from scaffold only — never from ladders or unstable surfaces during spall removal.
Check scaffold stability and guardrails in place before starting work each shift.
Use vibration-damping gloves during extended grinding or impact tool use.
Contain and sweep spalled concrete and dust daily — do not allow accumulation.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start grinding until: dust extraction system tested and running or wet method confirmed active
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not begin work at height until: scaffold inspection certificate current and posted on site
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: respiratory protection damaged, dislodged, or worker reports difficulty breathing
🛑 STOP WORK if: angle grinder guard missing, wheel cracked, or vibration increases suddenly
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold guardrail damaged or worker loses balance or near-miss occurs
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Brief all workers on spall removal sequence, scaffold entry points, and dust control method before work starts.
Assign dedicated spotter if working at heights above 2 m or near occupied areas below.
Record daily tool checks (grinder guard, RCD, leads) in site logbook.
Schedule dust monitoring or personal air sampling if grinding extends beyond 4 hours per day.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: P2 or P3 respiratory protection (half-mask or full-face)
Hearing protection (earplugs or muffs if grinder noise exceeds 85 dB)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.evidence: Worker confirms fit-test record current; supervisor observes correct mask seating; site logbook entry dated and signed

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.task: Latent conditions check — stop work if toxic materials encountered
tasks.scope: Pre-existing toxic materials (lead paint, asbestos) are latent conditions subject to additional cost — deemed variation per contract. If suspect material is found, stop work and notify supervisor.
hazards: Exposure to pre-existing toxic materials (lead paint, asbestos) if disturbed during remedial works
tasks.dominant_hazard: asbestos fibre inhalation from disturbance during survey
controls: Stop work immediately if suspect material (e.g. fibrous board, flaking paint on pre-1970 surfaces) is encountered
Do not disturb, sample, or remove any suspect material
Notify supervisor and site manager — arrange licensed assessment before resuming
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not resume work in affected area until licensed assessor has cleared the material
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any suspect fibrous, powdery, or flaking material is disturbed or exposed
admin: Brief all workers at induction: if you see suspect material, stop and report
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) (or higher if friable ACM suspected)

monitoring.critical_control: SDS on site, PPE matched to chemical, ventilation confirmed
monitoring.frequency: at induction and start of each new work area
monitoring.evidence: Inspection log, photographs, no visible disturbance marks or dust at suspect areas, marked areas intact
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Workers can describe stop-work trigger; no suspect material disturbed

responsibility.SUP: Brief crew on latent conditions, stop work if suspect material found, arrange assessment
responsibility.WKR: Report any suspect material immediately, do not disturb or sample

tasks.task: Paint exterior masonry, render, eaves, and soffits
tasks.scope: Apply primer and finish coats to brickwork, render, fibre cement eaves, and soffits per specification and colour schedule.
hazards: fall from height if worker loses balance on scaffold or platform during painting
eye or skin irritation from paint splash or overspray
inhalation of paint fumes or solvent vapour in poorly ventilated conditions
slip hazard on scaffold platforms from wet paint or spilled paint product
controls: Wear fall arrest harness and lanyard clipped to secure anchor point before accessing scaffold above 2 m.
Check scaffold is tagged safe, platforms are level, and guardrails are in place before starting work.
Wear eye protection
Ventilate work area with fans or open doors to reduce solvent vapour and fume exposure.
Wipe spilled paint from scaffold platforms immediately with cloth before it dries.
Use drop sheets or containment to catch paint drips and prevent slip hazards.
Keep paint container and solvent bottles secure and upright on scaffold to prevent spill.
Stop work and move to fresh air if dizziness, headache, or breathing difficulty occurs.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start painting until: scaffold inspection certificate is displayed and all workers briefed on fall arrest and paint hazards.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: harness, lanyard, or anchor point is damaged or missing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold guardrails are loose, missing, or platforms are wet and slippery.
🛑 STOP WORK if: paint fume odour is strong and ventilation fans are not operating.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm all workers hold current White Card before site induction.
Brief team on paint type, solvent content, and emergency response for spills or exposure.
Record scaffold inspection date and tag number in site diary.
Provide MSDS for all paints and solvents accessible on site.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Respirator (if ventilation is insufficient and fume odour is present)

monitoring.critical_control: SDS on site, PPE matched to chemical, ventilation confirmed
monitoring.frequency: before each shift and after any break over 30 minutes
monitoring.evidence: Worker confirms harness clip-point visually; supervisor observes and signs site diary.

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold and fall arrest systems, enforce exclusion zone, check SDS
responsibility.WKR: Use harness and lanyard, wear respiratory protection, report faults

tasks.task: Paint timber doors, frames, and treat timber beams
tasks.scope: Sand and prepare timber; apply primer, undercoat, and finish to doors and frames; apply protective treatment to exposed timber beams
hazards: eye or skin irritation from paint or timber treatment product splash
inhalation of paint or treatment fumes in enclosed spaces or poor ventilation
minor cut or abrasion from sanding sharp edges or splinters during timber preparation
fall from height if work is carried out on upper-level doors or exposed beams from scaffold
tasks.dominant_hazard: inhalation of fumes or fall from height if at elevation
controls: Wear respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) or powered unit) when sanding timber or applying paint in enclosed spaces.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection, primer, or timber treatment products.
make sure work area has natural or mechanical ventilation before starting paint application.
Secure all scaffold or work platform before climbing to access upper-level doors or beams.
Sand timber on flat surfaces using dust-extraction equipment or damp-sand method to control dust.
Apply paint or treatment in thin coats, allowing full drying time between coats as per product datasheet.
Do not leave paint or treatment containers open; recap immediately after use.
Wipe skin or eyes with clean water immediately if paint or treatment splash occurs.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply paint until: ventilation is active and air flow confirmed across work area
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not work at height until: scaffold or access platform tagged safe and load-bearing capacity verified
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: respiratory protection fails or becomes saturated with dust or fumes
🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation system stops or air flow drops to stagnant
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold or access platform shows movement, cracking, or instability at height
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Review product safety datasheets for all paints, primers, and timber treatments before work start.
Brief all workers on location of spill kit, eyewash station, and emergency procedures.
Establish exclusion zone below elevated work to prevent public exposure to falling tools or debris.
Record ventilation system status and air flow checks at start of each shift.
check scaffold tagging and load certification daily before first worker climbs.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Respiratory protection — P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) or powered respirator (paint fumes, dust)
Protective footwear — closed-toe leather (dropped tools or splinters)
Overalls or work wear (skin protection from splashes)

monitoring.critical_control: SDS on site, PPE matched to chemical, ventilation confirmed
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start and before climbing to height
monitoring.evidence: Worker verbal confirmation of fit-test, visual check of mask seal, observation of airflow indicators on powered units

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold and fall arrest systems, enforce exclusion zone, check SDS
responsibility.WKR: Use harness and lanyard, wear respiratory protection, report faults

tasks.task: Seal unpainted brick and concrete surfaces
tasks.scope: Apply appropriate sealer to unpainted brick and concrete areas to protect against moisture and weathering.
hazards: eye or skin irritation from sealer splash or contact
inhalation of sealer fumes or solvent vapour during application
slip hazard from excess sealer or wet surfaces on scaffold platforms
fall from height if sealing work at elevated locations on scaffold
tasks.dominant_hazard: fall from height or inhalation of sealer fumes
controls: Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection
Apply sealer in well-ventilated areas or with mechanical ventilation running continuously.
Use respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum) if fumes cause eye or throat irritation.
Lay drop sheets or absorbent material on scaffold platforms below sealing work.
Apply sealer with brush or roller to control splashing and drips.
Wipe excess sealer from scaffold deck and handrails immediately to prevent slip hazard.
Establish exclusion zone below sealing work; prohibit foot traffic until sealer dries.
Check scaffold stability and guardrails secure before starting work at height.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start sealing until: mechanical ventilation confirmed running or outdoor wind speed adequate
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker experiences dizziness, nausea, or respiratory distress during application
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold shows signs of movement, damage, or instability during or after sealing
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain product safety data sheet (SDS) for sealer before work starts.
Brief all workers on sealer hazards, application method, and ventilation requirements.
Confirm rescue procedures in place if working at height on scaffold.
Record sealer product, batch number, application area, and workers present on site log.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) or higher (if fumes present or SDS indicates)

monitoring.critical_control: Check ventilation running and worker respiratory condition each 30 minutes.
monitoring.frequency: continuous during application and 60 minutes post-application
monitoring.evidence: Ventilation equipment running log; worker sign-off on symptom check; photographic record of drop sheets and exclusion zone.

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold and fall arrest systems, enforce exclusion zone, check SDS
responsibility.WKR: Use harness and lanyard, wear respiratory protection, report faults

tasks.scope: Install new green wall substrate, frames, and planting system per design and specification
hazards: fall from height if worker loses balance on scaffold during frame installation or planting
struck by falling frame components, substrate panels, or fixings during installation
eye or minor laceration injury from handling sharp fixing brackets or metal frames
strain injury from manual handling of heavy substrate panels or planter boxes
controls: Wear fall arrest harness and lanyard clipped to approved anchor point before working at height.
Install frames from stable scaffold platform with guard rails and toe boards in place.
Check all substrate panels and frames for damage before installation.
Use two workers minimum to handle and position substrate panels over 15 kg.
Wear eye protection
Barricade work area below installation zone to prevent struck-by incidents.
Secure all loose fixings and fasteners in containers before working at height.
Brief all workers on fall hazards and emergency rescue procedure before starting work.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker is working at height without harness clipped to approved anchor
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold guard rails or toe boards are missing or damaged
🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate panel or frame component is dropped or falls from height
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Record daily toolbox talk covering fall prevention and rescue procedure.
Confirm building occupant notification completed before work starts each day.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone marked, barriers in place, no pedestrians below work area
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation log or supervisor sign-off sheet — harness and anchor point checked each time

responsibility.SUP: Verify fall protection, check module weights, sign off hold points
responsibility.WKR: Wear fall harness, check lanyard attachment, report equipment damage

tasks.scope: Remove scaffold or EWP system; clear site debris and make good; remove barriers and signage; restore common areas.
hazards: fall from height during scaffold dismantling if worker loses balance or scaffold becomes unstable
fall of scaffold components onto persons below or on ground level during dismantling
crush injury if scaffold components land on foot or hand during lowering or removal
struck by vehicle during debris removal or site egress if work area overlaps traffic zone
tasks.dominant_hazard: fall from height or collapse during dismantling
controls: Confirm scaffold tag current and structure stable before starting dismantling work.
Work from top to bottom; remove components in reverse erection order.
Barricade ground zone beneath scaffold to 1.5 m radius; prohibit entry during dismantling.
Secure each removed component to prevent rolling or sliding during lowering.
Lower components by rope or sling to designated drop zone; do not throw or drop.
Wear high-visibility vest and hard hat always during dismantling and debris removal.
Check debris area clear of persons before moving vehicle or operating mobile plant.
Remove temporary barriers, signs, and isolation tape only after final safety sweep complete.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove ground-level barriers until: all debris collected, ground zone clear of hazards, and final safety check recorded.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold shows visible damage, rust, leaning, or instability during dismantling.
🛑 STOP WORK if: personnel or vehicles present in barricaded ground zone during component lowering.
🛑 STOP WORK if: weather conditions (wind >40 km/h, rain, poor visibility) prevent safe dismantling or debris handling.
admin: Confirm all utilities (electricity, gas, water, telecommunications) isolated and certified disconnected before dismantling.
Establish exclusion zone signage (min 2 m radius) and brief all personnel on ground zone restrictions.
Record daily scaffold condition check and dismantling progress; confirm final all-clear and site make-good sign-off in project log.
ppe: Respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested)) during damp-wipe and sweeping of silica dust

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start and before each major dismantling phase
monitoring.evidence: Supervisor sign-off on daily site log; photographic record of scaffold condition; removal checklist completed and retained.

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

Asbestos Removal Licence — if ACM identified in pre-demolition survey
SDS training — epoxy resins, chemical anchors, concrete admixtures
Working at heights — verified current competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent per current RII Training Package)
EWP operator licence — WP class where boom exceeds 11m

Rescue equipment — on site and ready for immediate deployment before any elevated work starts

Wet cutting method — preferred over dry cutting to suppress dust
On-tool extraction — vacuum with H-class filter where wet method not practicable
Lot boundary — confirm lot vs common property boundary before any work

regulatory_notes: WHS Reg 2017 s.292 — demolition SWMS required before work
Pre-demolition hazardous materials survey mandatory
Structural engineer — signed shoring plan required
WHS Reg 2017 r.291-297 — structural alterations and temporary support obligations
SafeWork NSW Code of Practice: Demolition Work
Pre-demolition survey — must identify ACM, lead paint, PCB, synthetic mineral fibre, and structural hazards
Robotic demolition — where space confined or structural collapse risk elevated; operator remains outside exclusion zone
Progressive demolition — top-down sequence unless engineer specifies otherwise
Overhead powerlines — request de-energisation before demolition plant operates within exclusion zone
Dust suppression — water suppression mandatory during demolition; not optional for urban sites
Waste management — hazardous demolition waste (ACM, lead, PCB) must be segregated and disposed per EPA license requirements
AS 3600 — Concrete structures — repair must match original structural intent
Silica dust — P2 respirator mandatory for all grinding and cutting
Epoxy products — 2-part systems, strict pot life management
WHS Reg 2017 Part 4.4 — fall prevention hierarchy applies to all fall risk
SafeWork NSW Code of Practice: Managing the Risk of Falls at Workplaces
Harness inspection — pre-use check logged before each shift
WHS Reg 2017 r.305 — rescue procedure required before commencing work at height
Suspension trauma — incapacitated worker must be lowered within 15 minutes; harness straps can cause positional asphyxia
Emergency contacts — on-site personnel trained in rescue procedure before elevated work begins
WHS Reg 2017 r.291-303 — fall prevention hierarchy: (1) eliminate, (2) passive edge protection/guardrail, (3) restraint system, (4) fall arrest, (5) administrative
Edge protection first — guardrails preferred over harness where work area permits fixed barriers
Control line — 2m setback from edge, used only when guardrail not practicable
Exclusion zone required below WAH operations — size proportional to fall/drop zone; physical barrier where practicable, flagging/bunting as minimum
Emergency access must be maintained to all work zones including WAH exclusion zones
Strata schemes — notify strata manager and obtain by-law compliance
Noise curfew — residential: 8am–5pm weekdays, 8am–1pm Saturday, no Sunday
Dust — full hoarding required where public or occupant exposure possible
WHS Reg 2017 s.49 — WES for respirable crystalline silica 0.05 mg/m³
Engineered stone — banned in NSW workplaces from 1 July 2024
Health monitoring — mandatory where regular silica exposure occurs
Common property — owners corporation owns and is responsible for common property
By-laws — non-compliance can result in NCAT order to make good
AS 3700 — Masonry Structures
Masonry mortar curing period — 3-7 days after application; highest risk of collapse during this period
Freestanding walls without returns or cross-walls — require engineer-assessed temporary bracing
Temporary bracing must withstand likely wind forces for the specific site and stage of construction
Wall height, reduced mortar strength, and wind forces must all be considered in the bracing design
Steel reinforcement and core filling as construction progresses is an accepted bracing method
